title: Frontend: Implement Garbage Collector
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Implement Garbage Collector. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({objects,roots}). Objects are {id,refs}; IDs are unique strings. Mark reachable objects from roots and return sorted {survivors,collected}. Unknown roots throw Unknown root; references to unallocated IDs throw Dangling reference. Unreachable cycles must be collected. This is a heap graph simulation.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent heap objects as IDs with outgoing references and provide an explicit root set.
alternativeApproaches: Add an incremental marking model and state the write-barrier invariant needed when the graph changes during marking.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Reachable cycle; unreachable cycle; no roots.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
